# Supersymmetric Solutions of N=2, D=4 Minimal Supergravity

The supersymmetric solutions of N=2, D=4 minimal supergravity, in both its ungauged and gauged versions, can be systematically classified according to the fraction of supersymmetry that they preserve. This classification distinguishes between solutions preserving different amounts of the original supersymmetry, most notably the 1/4- and 1/2-supersymmetric configurations. Organizing the solutions in this way provides a clear and structured understanding of the space of supersymmetric backgrounds admitted by these theories.

The classification is carried out using spinorial geometry techniques. This approach exploits the properties of the Killing spinors directly, employing a description of spinors in terms of differential forms together with a judicious use of gauge symmetries to bring the spinors into canonical representative forms. The method allows one to analyze the constraints imposed by the Killing spinor equations in a systematic and geometrically transparent manner, making it particularly well suited to the problem of classifying solutions by their preserved supersymmetry.

Within this framework, and subject to a single reasonable assumption in the 1/2-supersymmetric time-like case of the gauged theory, it is possible to derive the complete form of all supersymmetric solutions. This means that, aside from this one assumption, the analysis yields an exhaustive description of the geometries and associated matter fields consistent with the requirement of preserved supersymmetry, thereby giving a comprehensive picture of the supersymmetric sector of both the ungauged and gauged theories.

Beyond recovering the previously known configurations, the results uncovered by this analysis include a number of new 1/4- and 1/2-supersymmetric solutions. These novel backgrounds enrich the known landscape of supersymmetric solutions and demonstrate that the classification is capable of revealing structures that had not been identified in earlier treatments.

Among these new possibilities are particularly striking examples: gravitational waves propagating on bubbles of nothing in AdS₄. These solutions combine the non-trivial topology characteristic of bubble-of-nothing geometries with the presence of gravitational wave excitations, all within an asymptotically anti-de Sitter setting. Their existence highlights the richness of the supersymmetric solution space of gauged N=2, D=4 supergravity and offers interesting avenues for further study in the context of holography and the stability of anti-de Sitter spacetimes.

# Supersymmetric Solutions of N=2, D=4 Minimal Supergravity via Spinorial Geometry

## Overview

Supersymmetric solutions play a central role in our understanding of supergravity theories, serving as stable backgrounds around which quantum corrections are often under better control, and providing crucial arenas for the study of black holes, cosmological configurations, and holographic dualities. In this work, we undertake a systematic classification of the supersymmetric solutions of N=2, D=4 minimal supergravity, treating both the ungauged and the gauged versions of the theory. The gauged case is of particular interest because its bosonic sector admits an anti-de Sitter (AdS_4) vacuum, thereby connecting our analysis to the broader context of AdS/CFT correspondence and lower-dimensional holography.

## Methodology: Spinorial Geometry

Our approach relies on the techniques of spinorial geometry, a framework that exploits an explicit oscillator basis for spinors together with the gauge freedom afforded by the local symmetry group of the theory. By bringing the Killing spinors into simple canonical forms using this residual gauge symmetry, one can reduce the Killing spinor equations to a tractable system of algebraic and differential conditions on the bosonic fields. This method offers a powerful and structured alternative to more traditional bilinear or G-structure approaches, and it is especially well suited to a classification organized according to the number of preserved supersymmetries.

## Classification by Fraction of Preserved Supersymmetry

The core of our analysis is the classification of solutions according to the fraction of supersymmetry they preserve. In N=2, D=4 minimal supergravity, the relevant fractions are 1/4 (a single preserved supersymmetry, corresponding to four supercharges reduced to one) and 1/2 (two preserved supersymmetries), together with the maximally supersymmetric backgrounds. For each case we determine the geometric constraints imposed on the spacetime and on the graviphoton field strength.

A standard organizing principle in such classifications is the distinction between the *time-like* and *null* cases, determined by the causal character of the vector field constructed as a Killing spinor bilinear. We give particular attention to the 1/2-supersymmetric time-like class, where, under a reasonable and clearly stated technical assumption, we succeed in deriving the complete explicit form of all admissible solutions. This provides a closed and exhaustive local description of these highly symmetric backgrounds.

## New Solutions and Physical Implications

Beyond systematizing the known solution landscape, our classification uncovers several previously unknown configurations, both in the 1/4- and the 1/2-supersymmetric sectors. Among the most striking of these are gravitational wave solutions propagating on *bubbles of nothing* in AdS_4. Bubbles of nothing are smooth, geodesically complete spacetimes in which a compact spatial direction smoothly closes off, effectively removing a region of the geometry; their embedding in a supersymmetric AdS_4 setting, dressed with a gravitational wave profile, represents a genuinely new class of backgrounds.

These findings enrich the catalog of admissible supergravity configurations and highlight the effectiveness of spinorial geometry techniques in exposing solutions that had escaped earlier, less systematic treatments. The new bubble and wave solutions in particular may have interesting implications for questions of vacuum stability, the structure of the AdS landscape, and the interplay between supersymmetry and non-trivial spacetime topology.

## Conclusion

Taken together, our results provide a comprehensive and organized picture of the supersymmetric sector of N=2, D=4 minimal supergravity in both its ungauged and gauged forms. By classifying solutions according to the fraction of preserved supersymmetry and completing the description of the 1/2-supersymmetric time-like case, and by exhibiting new 1/4- and 1/2-supersymmetric solutions—including gravitational waves on bubbles of nothing in AdS_4—this work meaningfully expands the known landscape of four-dimensional supergravity backgrounds.

# The Subject of This Conversation

Every meaningful exchange begins with a choice: what will we talk about? **The** first step in any discussion, essay, or casual conversation is deciding on **the** subject. Without it, words drift aimlessly, lacking the anchor that gives them purpose and direction.

## Why the Subject Matters

**The** subject is the heart of communication. It tells the listener or reader where our attention is focused, and it shapes everything that follows. When we say, "This is important," we are pointing toward something specific—**this** particular idea, **this** moment, **this** thought that deserves our shared focus.

Consider how often small words carry great weight. "The" narrows our attention to something definite. "This" brings an idea close, making it immediate and present. Together, these humble words allow us to build clarity out of chaos, transforming scattered notions into organized meaning.

## Choosing the Right Subject

Not every topic deserves equal treatment. The best writers and speakers learn to select **the** subject carefully, asking themselves:

- Is **this** topic worth exploring?
- Does **the** subject connect with my audience?
- Will **this** idea leave a lasting impression?

By pausing to reflect on these questions, we ensure that our words serve a purpose rather than filling empty space.

## Conclusion

In the end, **this** simple truth remains: communication thrives when we know our subject and honor it with clear, deliberate language. **The** next time you begin to write or speak, remember that **this** choice—the subject you embrace—will define everything that comes after.

# Abstract

We present a systematic classification of supersymmetric solutions in minimal N=2, D=4 gauged and ungauged supergravity using the spinorial geometry method. By employing the gauge symmetry of the theory to bring Killing spinors into canonical forms, we reduce the analysis of the Killing spinor equations to a set of algebraic and differential conditions on the spacetime geometry and the graviphoton field strength. We consider both cases distinguished by the isotropy group of the Killing spinor within Spin(3,1), corresponding to solutions preserving either N=1 (quarter-BPS) or N=2 (half-BPS) of the supersymmetry.

For the ungauged theory, we recover and refine the well-known distinction between the timelike and null classes of solutions, showing how the spinorial geometry approach naturally reproduces the Israel–Wilson–Perjés and pp-wave families. In the gauged case, where a negative cosmological constant is present, we demonstrate how the Killing spinor equations constrain the geometry to admit a canonical fibration, with the base space geometry determined by a combination of Kähler and monopole-type conditions. We derive the complete set of integrability conditions and show that, together with the Bianchi identity and the graviphoton equation of motion, supersymmetry implies all remaining field equations up to a single additional component.

Our results provide a unified geometric framework for constructing and understanding BPS black holes, cosmic strings, and gravitational wave solutions in four-dimensional minimal supergravity, and clarify the interplay between preserved supersymmetry and the underlying spacetime structure.

## General Framework and Common Results

### Classification of Supersymmetric Solutions

A central achievement in this field is the **systematic classification** of solutions preserving some fraction of supersymmetry. Key techniques include:

- **Killing spinor analysis**: Solutions are characterized by the existence of spinors satisfying the vanishing of supersymmetry variations (gravitino, gaugino, etc.)
- **G-structure methods**: The bilinears constructed from Killing spinors define geometric structures on spacetime that constrain the metric and matter fields
- **Spinorial geometry**: A powerful approach using explicit spinor representations to solve the Killing spinor equations

### Ungauged Supergravity

For $\mathcal{N}=2$ ungauged supergravity, typical results include:

- **Timelike case**: Solutions describe stationary configurations, including the important class of **BPS black holes** with metrics of the Israel-Wilson-Perjés type
- **Null case**: Yields **pp-wave** and related null solutions
- Supersymmetric black holes satisfy **attractor mechanism** equations, where scalar fields flow to fixed values at horizons determined by charges

### Gauged Supergravity

Adding gauging (introducing a scalar potential via a cosmological constant or gauge coupling) modifies results significantly:

- Solutions are often **asymptotically Anti-de Sitter (AdS)** rather than flat
- New classes emerge including **AdS black holes**, **magnetic solutions**, and **rotating configurations**
- Relevant to the **AdS/CFT correspondence** and holographic applications
- BPS bounds and mass formulas are modified by the cosmological constant

| Asymptotics | Flat | AdS |

| Preserved SUSY | 1/2, 1/4 BPS | Various fractions |
| Applications | Black hole entropy | Holography, CFT duals |

## Abstract

We investigate the fractions of supersymmetry preserved by bosonic backgrounds in minimal supergravity theories across various dimensions, with particular emphasis on the structure of Killing spinor solutions and their classification. Beginning from the framework of $\mathcal{N}=1$ supergravity in four dimensions and its higher-dimensional analogues, we analyze the conditions under which supersymmetric configurations preserve fractions $\nu = k/N$ of the total supersymmetry, where $k$ counts the number of independent Killing spinors admitted by a given background. Employing the spinorial geometry approach and the theory of $G$-structures, we systematically enumerate the allowed values of $\nu$ and demonstrate how the isotropy groups of Killing spinors within the relevant Spin group constrain the admissible fractions. Our analysis reveals that certain fractions, notably those exceeding one-half, impose stringent integrability conditions that force the geometry toward maximally symmetric or homogeneous spaces. We further establish relationships between the preserved supersymmetry fraction and the underlying holonomy reduction, showing that backgrounds preserving exotic fractions correspond to special geometric structures not realized in generic compactifications. These results provide a unified classification scheme applicable to black hole solutions, domain walls, and cosmological backgrounds, and clarify the interplay between preserved supersymmetry, the equations of motion, and the associated Bianchi identities. We conclude by discussing implications for the moduli space of supersymmetric vacua and potential extensions to gauged supergravity theories with nontrivial scalar potentials.

---

# Abstract

We present a systematic classification of supersymmetric solutions in four-dimensional gauged supergravity, organized according to the fraction of preserved supersymmetry. Working within the framework of $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauged supergravity coupled to vector and hypermultiplets, we employ the spinorial geometry method and G-structure techniques to constrain the allowed backgrounds. Solutions are catalogued into distinct classes preserving $1/2$, $1/4$, and $1/8$ of the supersymmetry, with the residual holonomy and associated Killing spinor equations analyzed for each sector.

A central result of our analysis is the discovery of a novel family of supersymmetric gravitational wave solutions propagating on bubbles of nothing in asymptotically AdS$_4$ spacetimes. These configurations describe pp-wave deformations superposed on the smooth capping geometry that resolves the would-be singularity, preserving a minimal fraction of supersymmetry while remaining geodesically complete. We demonstrate that the wave profiles satisfy a generalized Laplace equation on the transverse space, with the AdS radius entering as a mass-like parameter that governs the falloff behavior near the conformal boundary.

We further examine the holographic interpretation of these bubble-wave geometries, discussing their role as non-perturbative decay channels and the constraints imposed by supersymmetry on their stability. Our classification unifies previously known BPS solutions—including domain walls, black holes, and cosmic strings—within a common structural framework, and clarifies the interpolation between distinct BPS sectors. We comment on possible embeddings into eleven-dimensional supergravity and the implications for the swampland program.
